summary: Backend-only verification of AMASS Phase 3 (Marketing & Sharing / share_routes.py). 20/20 pytest cases pass (0 failed, 0 skipped) covering property + agent share bundles, WhatsApp URL construction, share event recording (auth-gated, all 5 required channels), stats permission model (owner + admin override + 403 for non-owner), URL-encoding round-trip, bulk-event idempotency, and the requested regression sweep (plans, subscription/me, public agent, badge progress). One documented minor gap: GET /api/properties/{id} does not surface the denormalised share_count / share_by_channel counters — clients must call /api/share/property/{id}/stats. No blocking bugs.

minor.issue: share_count and share_by_channel are $inc'd into the Mongo document by POST /api/share/property/{id}/event, but the Property Pydantic response_model filters them out so the standard property fetch never exposes the counters. Review spec (#3) explicitly asks for verification via GET /api/properties/{id}. Either (a) add both fields to Property/PropertyOut (Optional[int] and Optional[dict]) or (b) update the spec to source counters exclusively from /api/share/property/{id}/stats. The stats endpoint is currently the only working read path.

action_items: Optional: extend the Property response model (server.py) to include share_count: Optional[int]=0 and share_by_channel: Optional[dict]=None so the counters are visible from GET /api/properties/{id} as the review spec expects. Not blocking — the /stats endpoint already returns them correctly.
critical_code_review_comments: share_routes.py: registrations of the ShareEventIn.channel Literal align with the review spec (whatsapp/qr/copy_link/native_share/flyer/email/sms) — good.
record_property_share / record_agent_share both denormalise counters via $inc and also insert a raw share_events audit row — correct dual-write; no ObjectId leak, all endpoints project {_id: 0}.
property_share_stats correctly enforces owner-or-admin permission (403 for non-owner, 200 for admin override) — verified in tests.
WhatsApp deep link uses urllib.parse.quote which preserves \n as %0A — decoded text is byte-identical to whatsapp_message (verified in test_whatsapp_url_encoded_matches_message).
flyer_payload.property.images is correctly sliced to 1 cover image and amenities to max 6 — matches spec.

Minor: no rate-limiting on POST /event — a hostile client can spam counter increments unbounded. Consider a per-user+target+channel throttle (e.g. 1/min) or dedup via unique index on (user_id, target_id, channel, minute-bucket). Not part of this iteration's scope but flagged.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_share_routes.py (new pytest suite; no production code touched)
seed_data_creation: Created 1 TEST_ foreign property owned by an ephemeral registered user (TEST_share_<uuid>@example.com) so the admin-override stats test could execute. Cleanup not performed — the test property carries the TEST_ prefix and is on the fresh user's account (agent_id != demo). Recommend a scheduled cleanup or leave for future iterations to overwrite.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The share_routes.py module is fully functional end-to-end. Pytest suite at /app/backend/tests/test_share_routes.py is idempotent (uses relative deltas via /stats baseline, not hard-coded absolutes) and safe to re-run. Auth uses access_token (not token) in the login/register response. Note: pytest.ini enforces `-n 2 --dist loadscope`; override with `-o "addopts=-n 0"` when running just this file to avoid worker contention on the shared demo property. All 10 seed properties are owned by demo — foreign_property fixture auto-creates one via a fresh user (Starter plan allows first 5 free).
